summary: Specifies the Active Users service, which sends a list of the currently active users on the host without regard to the input. It is an Internet Standard for hosts that choose to implement it.

eli5.summary: A computer you can ask who is currently using it, like peeking at a sign-in sheet.

subtitle: A service on port 11 that lists who is currently logged in to a host.

tldr.problem: Engineers want a simple way to see which users are logged in on a remote host, as a debugging and measurement aid.
tldr.mechanism: A server on port 11 sends a list of the currently active users over TCP and closes the connection, or sends the list in one or more UDP datagrams. Received data is ignored.
tldr.outcome: The RFC is an Internet Standard for hosts that choose to implement it. The list has no required syntax, but each user should be on a separate line.

today: RFC 866 is an Internet Standard and has not been obsoleted or updated, so it remains the definition of the Active Users service.

sections.title: An Active Users Service
sections.content:
RFC 866 defines the Active Users service. The RFC calls it a useful debugging and measurement tool that simply sends a list of the currently active users on the host without regard to the input.

An active user is one who is logged in, such as listed in SYSTAT or WHO. Hosts that choose to implement the protocol are expected to adopt this standard.
sections.eli5: It is a machine that tells you the names of everyone logged in, no matter what you ask it.

sections.title: The TCP and UDP Services
sections.content:
Over TCP, a server listens on TCP port 11. Once a connection is established it sends the list of active users and discards any data it receives. The service then closes the connection.

Over UDP, a server listens on UDP port 11 and answers each received datagram with a list of active users, ignoring the received data. If the list does not fit in one datagram, the server sends a sequence of datagrams but must not break a user's line across two of them. The user side should wait for a timeout for all datagrams to arrive, and they are not necessarily in order.
sections.eli5: If the list is too long for one note, the machine sends several notes. Each name stays whole on one note, and the notes may arrive mixed up.

sections.title: User List Syntax
sections.content: There is no specific syntax for the user list. The RFC recommends limiting it to the ASCII printing characters, space, carriage return and line feed, with each user listed on a separate line.
sections.eli5: The list is plain text with one person per line, like names on a roll call.
